claim: On 2022-07-25 AWS Transfer Family added fully managed support for the AS2 protocol on servers, so you can create servers that send and receive information with trading partners inside or outside the AWS environment.
question: When did Transfer Family add AS2 support?

qualifiers.scope: Transfer Family servers using the AS2 protocol

evidence.quote: | Fully managed support for Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) file transfer protocol with Transfer Family servers | You can create servers that use the AS2 protocol for sending and receiving information to and from trading partners who are inside or outside the AWS environment. For more information, see [Configuring AS2](create-b2b-server.md).  | July 25, 2022 |

note: d25-123. Older questions know only SFTP, FTPS and FTP.

claim: On 2023-07-25 AWS Transfer Family added SFTP connectors, which extend Transfer Family to communicate with remote servers both in the cloud and on premises.
question: When did Transfer Family add SFTP connectors?

evidence.quote: | Support for SFTP connectors | SFTP Connectors extend the capabilities of AWS Transfer Family to communicate with remote servers both in the cloud and on-premises. For more information, see [Using SFTP connectors](transfer-sftp-connectors.md). | July 25, 2023 |

claim: On 2024-01-16 Transfer Family began to provide static IP addresses for SFTP connectors and AS2, which enables connection with remote SFTP servers that are secured by IP allowlisting controls.
question: When did Transfer Family add static IP addresses for SFTP connectors?

evidence.quote: | Support for static IP addresses for SFTP connectors and AS2 | Transfer Family now provides static IP addresses for SFTP connectors and AS2. This enables connection with remote SFTP servers that are secured by IP allowlisting controls. For AS2, we're introducing static IP addresses for asynchronous MDN responses from AS2 servers. | January 16, 2024 |

claim: On 2024-02-08 Transfer Family began to automatically publish events to Amazon EventBridge for all file transfer operations.
question: When did Transfer Family start publishing events to Amazon EventBridge?

evidence.quote: | Integrate with Amazon EventBridge | AWS Transfer Family now automatically publishes events to Amazon EventBridge for all file transfer operations. For details, see [Managing Transfer Family events using Amazon EventBridge](eventbridge.md). | February 8, 2024 |

claim: On 2024-12-01 AWS Transfer Family added web apps, a resource that gives a simple interface for accessing data in Amazon S3 through a web browser.
question: When did Transfer Family add web apps?

evidence.quote: | Support for AWS Transfer Family web apps | AWS Transfer Family web apps are a new resource customers can use to create a simple interface for accessing their data in Amazon S3 through a web browser. For details, see [Transfer Family web apps](web-app.md). | December 1, 2024 |

claim: On 2025-06-30 Transfer Family began to support dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) endpoints for SFTP public endpoints, VPC-internal endpoints for SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2, SFTP and AS2 connectors, and API endpoints.
question: When did Transfer Family add IPv6 support, and for which endpoints?

qualifiers.scope: Transfer Family endpoints, connectors and API endpoints

evidence.quote: | IPv6 support | AWS Transfer Family now supports dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) endpoints for SFTP public endpoints, VPC-internal endpoints for SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2, SFTP and AS2 connectors, and API endpoints. For details, see [IPv6 support for Transfer Family servers](ipv6-support.md). | June 30, 2025 |

claim: On 2025-10-14 Transfer Family SFTP connectors began to support connecting to remote SFTP servers through your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).
question: When did Transfer Family SFTP connectors gain VPC-based connectivity?

evidence.quote: AWS Transfer Family SFTP connectors can now connect to remote SFTP servers through your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

evidence.heading: AWS Transfer Family SFTP connectors now support VPC-based connectivity

claim: On 2025-11-19 Transfer Family web apps began to support VPC hosted endpoints, so you can host the web app endpoint inside a virtual private cloud for private data transfers to and from Amazon S3 without traversing the public internet.
question: When did Transfer Family web apps gain VPC endpoint support?

evidence.quote: | VPC endpoint support for Transfer Family web apps | AWS Transfer Family web apps now support VPC hosted endpoints, allowing you to host your web app endpoint inside a virtual private cloud for private data transfers to and from Amazon S3 without traversing the public internet. For details, see [Create a Transfer Family web app in a VPC](create-webapp-in-vpc.md). | November 19, 2025 |

claim: On 2026-01-26 AWS Transfer Family customers could access file system data stored in Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP over SFTP, FTPS and FTP.
question: When did Transfer Family add Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP support?

qualifiers.scope: Transfer Family access to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

evidence.quote: AWS Transfer Family customers can now access file system data stored in Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP over SFTP, FTPS, and FTP.

evidence.heading: AWS Transfer Family now supports Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

note: d25-123. Examinable but recent: Changed recently.

claim: On 2026-09-15 AWS Transfer Family SFTP servers behind a Network Load Balancer could use PROXY protocol v2 to preserve the client's source IP address. Before this, an NLB replaced the client's source IP with its own private IP address.
question: When could Transfer Family SFTP servers behind an NLB preserve the client's source IP?

values.display: replaced the client's source IP with its own private IP address

qualifiers.scope: SFTP servers with a VPC-hosted endpoint behind a Network Load Balancer

evidence.quote: | Source IP preservation for SFTP servers behind a Network Load Balancer | AWS Transfer Family SFTP servers behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB) can use PROXY protocol v2 to preserve the client's source IP address. IP-based access policies in your custom identity provider then see the real client address instead of the NLB private IP. For details, see [Working with Network Load Balancers](working-with-nlb.md). | September 15, 2026 |
Previously, an NLB replaced the client's source IP with its own private IP address, so your Transfer Family logs and events recorded the NLB's address instead of the client's source IP.

changed.was: replaced the client's source IP with its own private IP address

note: d25-123. Generally available after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet (RULINGS rule 7). The What's New post is dated 2026-09-17.

claim: On 2026-09-30 AWS Transfer Family began to automatically approve requests to increase the SFTP connector quota up to 1,000 connectors per AWS account in each AWS Region. The default quota remains 100, and before this all quota increases required manual approval.
question: Up to what number are SFTP connector quota increases approved automatically, and since when?

values.display: all quota increases required manual approval

qualifiers.scope: SFTP connectors per AWS account in each AWS Region
qualifiers.condition: automatic approval applies to connectors using service-managed or Amazon VPC Lattice egress; above 1,000 submit a higher quota request

evidence.quote: AWS Transfer Family now automatically approves requests to increase your SFTP connector quota up to 1,000 connectors per AWS account in each AWS Region.
Previously, all quota increases required manual approval.
The default quota remains 100 SFTP connectors per AWS account in each AWS Region, and you continue to request increases in the AWS Service Quotas console.

evidence.heading: AWS Transfer Family now automatically approves SFTP connector quota increases up to 1,000

changed.was: all quota increases required manual approval

note: d25-122, d25-123. Generally available after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet (RULINGS rule 7). Current default and adjustability: transfer-family-quota-sftp-connectors-per-account.

claim: On 2026-10-01 AWS Transfer Family began to let you choose a custom CloudWatch Logs log group for managed workflow execution logs. Before this, every workflow attached to a server sent its execution logs to that server's CloudWatch log group.
question: Can you choose a separate CloudWatch log group for a Transfer Family workflow, and since when?

values.display: every workflow attached to a Transfer Family server sent its execution logs to that server’s CloudWatch log group

qualifiers.scope: Transfer Family managed workflow execution logs

evidence.quote: AWS Transfer Family now lets you choose a custom log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for managed workflow execution logs.
Previously, every workflow attached to a Transfer Family server sent its execution logs to that server’s CloudWatch log group, so you could not set a separate log destination for each workflow.

changed.was: every workflow attached to a Transfer Family server sent its execution logs to that server’s CloudWatch log group

note: d25-123. Generally available after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet (RULINGS rule 7).
